name: SSC GD Constable
fullName: Staff Selection Commission – Constable (GD) in CAPFs, SSF, Assam Rifles (Rifleman GD) and NCB (Sepoy) Examination
eligibility: Class 10 (matriculation) pass; 18–23 years (with category relaxations); physical standards and PET apply

notification.summary: The SSC calendar scheduled the GD Constable 2027 notification for 30 Sep 2026 with applications into October and the CBT in Jan–Mar 2027; as of 10 Oct 2026 its release could not be confirmed (reports suggest it may slip into October). The previous (2026) cycle had ≈25,487 tentative vacancies.

importantDates.date: 30 Sep 2026 (release not confirmed at check time)

notification.source: https://www.pw.live/ssc/exams/ssc-gd-2027-notification (secondary report of SSC calendar; official notices at https://ssc.gov.in)

pattern.notes: Candidates choose English or Hindi for Part D. Questions are at matriculation level; the paper is available in English, Hindi and 13 regional languages. NCC certificate holders get bonus marks. Normalisation applies across shifts. This mock uses the English option for Part D.

trendAnalysis.summary: GD is the easiest SSC CBT, but with ~50 lakh applicants the cut-offs are high, so accuracy matters. Reasoning focuses on analogy, classification, series, coding, directions, blood relations and a few figure questions. Elementary Maths is arithmetic: number system, percentage, profit & loss, ratio, average, time-work, speed and basic mensuration. GK is static – history, polity, geography, science, culture and sports – with only a handful of current-affairs questions. English tests basic vocabulary and grammar plus a short passage.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the commission's published question-paper/response-sheet format and from shift-wise memory-based papers and topic-wise analyses published by coaching sites (Testbook, Adda247, PW, Careers360 day-wise analyses) for the 2024–2026 cycles, cross-checked against the writer's own knowledge of SSC papers. Live web fetches during this round returned only summary pages (SSC barred public discussion of 2025 papers), so question-type detail relies mainly on prior knowledge of the papers; frequencies are approximate per-shift counts. Figure-based (non-verbal) archetypes are recorded but only text-renderable variants are used for generated questions.

archetypes.pattern: Word-pair analogy (A : B :: C : ?) built on a semantic relation – worker : tool, product : raw material, organ : function, instrument : quantity measured, young one : animal; distractors are words of the same category that do not share the relation.

Number-pair/triad analogy where the second term comes from an arithmetic rule on the first (n² ± k, n³ ± k, ×k ± c, digit operations); often framed with two example pairs and a note to operate on whole numbers without splitting digits; distractors satisfy the rule for only one pair or come from ±1 slips.
Letter-cluster analogy (ABCD : EFGH :: ? ) where each letter moves by a fixed or alternating +/− shift or is replaced by its opposite letter (A↔Z); distractors differ in exactly one letter.
Odd-one-out among four words/objects by category or property (three belong to one class, e.g. instruments, organs, rivers of one state); the trap is a surface feature shared by the odd item.
Odd number / number-pair / triad out of four where three follow one arithmetic rule (squares, primes, (a, b, c) with c = a×b − k, divisibility); the odd option breaks the rule by a small margin.
Odd letter-cluster out of four where three clusters have the same positional gaps (e.g. +2, +3 or opposite-letter pairs) and one breaks the gap pattern.
Number series with one missing/next term following a two-step rule (×k + c, alternating operations, differences forming squares/primes or their own series).

Letter or alphanumeric cluster series (e.g. three-letter groups with each position advancing by its own increment, possibly mixed with numbers); find the next cluster; distractors shift one position wrongly.
Word → letter code by a positional rule (each letter shifted by +k/−k, alternate shifts, reversal then shift, or opposite letters); decode the rule from one example and encode a new word.

Word → number code from alphabet positions (sum of positions, sum × k, sum of reverse positions, number of letters × k); apply the rule to a new word; distractors use forward instead of reverse positions.
Sentence coding: two or three short sentences coded as groups of code words; identify the code of a given word by finding the common word/code between statements.
Verbal chain / introduction ('pointing to a photo…') blood relation: trace 3–4 links and name the relation; traps are gender assumptions and the paternal/maternal side.
Coded blood relations: symbols (A + B, A × B, A − B …) stand for relations; decode an expression to find how two people are related, or which expression makes a given relation true.

Walking path of 3–5 legs with left/right turns; find the shortest distance and/or direction from the start (often a Pythagorean triple); or the final facing direction after a sequence of left/right/clockwise turns; traps are direction after a 'right turn' and adding instead of subtracting legs.
Symbol substitution: '+' means '×', '−' means '÷' etc.; rewrite and evaluate an expression with BODMAS; distractors come from left-to-right evaluation.
Which two signs (or two numbers) must be interchanged to make a given equation correct; each option names a pair of signs to swap.
Missing term inside a number sequence (often the middle term) built from a mixed rule such as ×1 + 1, ×2 + 2, ×3 + 3 … or alternating × and +; find the term that replaces '?'.
Defined-operation missing number: from two or three solved examples (a ★ b = …) infer the rule (a² + b², (a + b)², a×b + a …) and apply it; distractors fit just one example.

Position from both ends: total in a row/class from two ranks, rank from the other end, persons between two people, or a short comparison chain (taller/older) to find who is at a rank; trap is ±1 counting.
Calendar: day of the week for a date given a reference date (odd-days counting across leap years) or after n days.
Clock angle between the hands at a given time (30H − 5.5M) or time when hands coincide/are opposite.
Mirror image of a clock time or of an alphanumeric/number string (vertical mirror on the right); time question solved by 11:60 − time.
A square sheet is folded once or twice and punched/cut; predict how it looks (number/position of holes) when unfolded.
Count triangles/squares in a figure built from a square or triangle with diagonals and mid-lines.

Ancient and medieval India: dynasty founders, capitals, rulers' titles, Buddhist/Jain councils, Delhi Sultanate/Mughal/Vijayanagara rulers, battles with years and administrative reforms; distractors are rulers of the same or adjacent dynasty.
Modern India and freedom struggle: founders of organisations/newspapers, INC sessions and presidents, movements with years, Governors-General and their acts.
Article-number question: which Article deals with a given provision (FR, DPSP, office, emergency, finance); distractors are nearby Article numbers.
Constitution-making, Preamble, amendments, schedules and parts with their subject matter (e.g. which Schedule/amendment added X); distractors are adjacent schedules/amendments.
Constitutional/statutory offices: appointment, qualification (age), tenure, removal, oath, and borrowed features of the Constitution.
Indian physical geography: rivers (origin, tributaries, states), lakes, passes, hills, national parks and their states.
Soils, crops, minerals, climate and resources of India (which soil/crop/mineral/region; seasons and winds).
World/physical geography: atmosphere layers, ocean currents, straits, planets, latitudes and landforms.
Banking and monetary policy: RBI instruments (repo, CRR, SLR), functions, institutions and their headquarters.
Economic concepts and planning: GDP/GNP, deficits, inflation measures, Five-Year Plans, taxes, government schemes and their launch.
Physics: SI units and instruments, and everyday phenomena (mirrors/lenses, dispersion, sound speed, heat, electricity).
Chemistry: common names/formulae of compounds, ores and alloys, acids in foods, pH, gases and periodic-table facts.
Human biology: vitamins/minerals and deficiency diseases, organs and glands, blood, diseases and their causative agents.
Plant biology and classification: tissues, photosynthesis, plant hormones, cell organelles, scientists behind classification.
Performing arts and festivals: classical/folk dances, festivals and fairs with their states, instruments and their maestros.
Temples, monuments and architectural styles with their builders/dynasties and locations.
Recent national/international events of the last 1–2 years: summits and hosts, missions, schemes and major appointments.
Sports: number of players, terms and trophies of a sport, venues, and recent Olympic/Asian Games/World Cup results involving India.
Defence/CAPF static GK: raising year, headquarters, mottos and borders guarded by forces, gallantry awards, missiles and military exercises.
Unit digit of a power/product or remainder of a large power on division (cyclicity); distractors are adjacent cycle values.
Divisibility and number properties: smallest digit/number to add or subtract for divisibility by 9, 11, 8, which number is divisible, count of factors, primes, or sum of numbers in a range.
HCF/LCM word problem: largest number dividing with given remainders, bells tolling together, least number leaving the same remainder, or HCF × LCM = product.
BODMAS simplification with fractions/decimals/brackets or 'value of ?' equations; distractors come from wrong operation order.
Basic/successive percentage: x% of a number, net effect of successive increases/decreases, or price rise vs consumption cut.
Percentage word problems: election votes, pass-fail marks, salary spent/saved; find the total or the difference.
Marked price above cost with a discount (or successive discounts) – find profit % or marked price.
Cost/selling price relation: profit % from CP and SP, CP from SP and gain %, CP of x items = SP of y items, two articles sold at the same price, or false-weight dealers.
Simple interest: find rate/time/principal from amounts, or the time to become n times.
Compound interest for 2–3 years, CI − SI difference, or half-yearly compounding.
Divide an amount in a given (sometimes fractional) ratio, or find shares/partnership profit.
Ratio change: number added/subtracted to change a ratio, combined ratio A : B : C, or mean/third proportional.
Average: simple or consecutive-number averages, inclusion/exclusion/replacement of a member (teacher's age, wrong entry corrected), or overlap of first-k and last-k averages.
Two/three workers with individual days; together, one leaves after some days, or efficiency ratio problems.
Pipes and cisterns (filling and emptying pipes together) or men-days (M₁D₁ = M₂D₂) proportionality.
Trains crossing a pole/platform/another train (same or opposite direction) with km/h ↔ m/s conversion.
Average speed for to-and-fro journeys, relative speed/chase problems, or boats and streams.
2-D mensuration: area/perimeter of rectangles, triangles (Heron's), circles and sectors, change in area with change in dimensions.
3-D mensuration: volume/surface area of cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere/hemisphere; melting and recasting.
Factual RC question on a 150–250-word passage: answer is stated in the passage; distractors use passage words with altered meaning.
Inference/main-idea/title RC question: choose the central theme or what the author implies.
Vocabulary/tone in context: synonym/antonym of a word used in the passage or the author's tone.
Cloze passage with five numbered blanks; each item tests contextual vocabulary, a connector or a preposition; distractors are near-synonyms that fail the collocation.
Single-sentence blank requiring the contextually correct word (collocation, near-synonym choice).
Single-sentence blank testing grammar – prepositions, articles, tense, conjunctions.
Synonym of a standalone or underlined word (moderate CGL-level vocabulary); distractors include antonyms and look-alike words.
Antonym of a standalone or underlined word; the trap option is a synonym of the given word.
Meaning of a common idiom/phrase (or the idiom that fits a sentence); distractors are literal readings.
One-word substitute for a descriptive phrase (persons, -cide, -phobia, -archy words); distractors are related words of the same family.
Select the correctly (or incorrectly) spelt word among four look-alike spellings (double letters, ie/ei, -ance/-ence).
Sentence split into 3–4 segments; error in subject–verb agreement, pronoun or noun number (each/one of/neither…nor, uncountable nouns).
Sentence split into segments; error in tense sequence, preposition, comparative/superlative, or conjunction pairs (hardly…when, no sooner…than).
Change active to passive (or vice versa) across tenses, including questions and modals; distractors change the tense.

resources.notes: SSC releases tentative answer keys with each candidate's response sheet on ssc.gov.in after the CBT for a limited period; final keys are published after results. There is no permanent official PYQ archive; memory-based papers come from coaching sites.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first.
Eye : See :: Tongue : ?
questions.explanation: The eye is used to see; the tongue is used to taste.

questions.question:
Select the number that is related to the third number in the same way as the second is related to the first.
6 : 36 :: 7 : ?
Select the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Triangle, square and rectangle are polygons with straight sides; a circle has no straight sides.

questions.question: Select the number that does not belong to the group.
questions.explanation: 8 = 2³, 27 = 3³ and 64 = 4³ are perfect cubes; 100 is not.

questions.question:
Select the number that will come next in the series.
1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ?
questions.explanation: Squares of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 … next is 6² = 36.

questions.question:
Select the number that will come next in the series.
7, 10, 16, 25, 37, ?
questions.explanation: Differences: 3, 6, 9, 12, so next difference is 15: 37 + 15 = 52.

questions.question:
Select the letter that will come next in the series.
Z, X, U, Q, ?
If FISH is written as GJTI in a certain code, how will BIRD be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: B→C, I→J, R→S, D→E.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'sky is blue' is written as 'ta na pa' and 'blue ink pot' is written as 'ka ta ri'. What is the code for 'blue'?
questions.explanation: 'blue' is the only word common to both sentences, and 'ta' is the only code common to both. So blue = ta.

questions.question: R is a woman. P is the sister of Q, and Q is the son of R. How is R related to P?
questions.explanation: Q is R's son and P is Q's sister, so P is also R's child. R is a woman, so R is P's mother.

questions.question: Sunil is facing South. He turns left and then turns left again. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: Facing South, a left turn faces East; another left turn faces North.

questions.question: If '+' means '−' and '−' means '+', what is the value of 25 + 10 − 5?
In a row of 25 children, Raju is 10th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?

Select the number that will come in place of the question mark (?).
3, 6, 18, 72, ?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 2, 3, 4, then 5: 72 × 5 = 360.

questions.question: How many times do the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock coincide in a day (24 hours)?
questions.explanation: The hands coincide once every 12/11 hours (≈65 5/11 minutes), i.e. 11 times in 12 hours, so 22 times in 24 hours.

questions.question: Who gave the slogan 'Do or Die' during the Quit India Movement?
questions.explanation: Gandhiji gave the call 'Do or Die' in his Quit India speech at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942.

questions.question: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and:
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in 1526, founding the Mughal Empire. Rana Sanga was defeated at Khanwa (1527).

questions.question: Who founded the Arya Samaj?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj.

questions.question: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces?
questions.explanation: Under Article 53(2), the supreme command of the Defence Forces is vested in the President.

questions.question: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.question: How many Schedules are there in the Constitution of India at present?
questions.explanation: The original Constitution had 8 Schedules; there are 12 now (the 12th was added by the 74th Amendment, 1992).

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the Election Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests superintendence of elections in the Election Commission. 280 = Finance Commission, 312 = All-India Services, 356 = President's Rule.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean.

questions.question: Which state of India is known as the 'Land of Five Rivers'?
questions.explanation: Punjab means 'land of five waters' (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej).

questions.question: The Narmada river does NOT flow through which of the following states?
questions.explanation: The Narmada rises at Amarkantak (MP), forms part of the MP–Maharashtra border and enters Gujarat before reaching the Arabian Sea. It does not flow through Rajasthan.

questions.question: In India, currency notes of all denominations except the one-rupee note are issued by:
questions.explanation: The RBI issues all banknotes except the ₹1 note, which is issued by the Government of India (Ministry of Finance).

questions.question: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror gives an erect, diminished image and a wider field of view.

questions.question: Which gas is commonly used in fire extinguishers?
questions.explanation: CO₂ is heavier than air, does not support combustion and cuts off oxygen from the fire.

questions.question: Which tissue in plants carries water from the roots to the leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward; phloem carries food.

questions.question: Which Central Armed Police Force primarily guards India's border with China?
questions.explanation: ITBP guards the India–China border. BSF guards the Pakistan and Bangladesh borders, SSB the Nepal and Bhutan borders, and Assam Rifles the Myanmar border.

questions.question: Which is the smallest prime number?
questions.explanation: 2 is the smallest (and only even) prime number; 1 is neither prime nor composite.

questions.question: What is the HCF of 36 and 84?
What is 25% of 360?
When a number is increased by 20%, it becomes 90. What is the number?
The cost price of 10 pens is equal to the selling price of 8 pens. What is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Let CP of 1 pen = ₹1. SP of 8 pens = ₹10, so SP of 1 pen = 1.25. Profit = 25%.

questions.question: The marked price of a bag is ₹600. A discount of 15% is given. What is the selling price?
What is the simple interest on ₹2,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years?
If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, what is A : C?
What is the average of 12, 15, 18, 21 and 24?
A tap can fill a tank in 6 hours and another tap can empty the full tank in 9 hours. If both taps are opened together on an empty tank, in how many hours will it be filled?
questions.explanation: Net filling per hour = 1/6 − 1/9 = 1/18. Time = 18 hours.

questions.question: A car covers 180 km in 3 hours. How long will it take to cover 300 km at the same speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = 60 km/h; 300 ÷ 60 = 5 hours.

questions.question: What is the volume of a cube whose edge is 5 cm?
questions.explanation: Volume = a³ = 125 cm³.

questions.question: The circumference of a circle is 44 cm. What is its area? (Take π = 22/7)
What is the sum of all natural numbers from 1 to 50?
A shopkeeper sells two articles at ₹990 each. On one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. What is his overall gain or loss?

Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
HAPPY
questions.explanation: Happy means joyful.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
RAPID
questions.explanation: Rapid means fast – swift.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
ANCIENT
questions.explanation: Ancient (very old) is opposite to modern.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
VICTORY
questions.explanation: The opposite of victory is defeat.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom.
To break the ice
options: To start a conversation and ease tension
questions.explanation: 'Break the ice' means to make people feel relaxed, especially by starting a conversation.

questions.question:
Select the one-word substitute for the given phrase.
A place where birds are kept
questions.explanation: Aviary = birds; apiary = bees; aquarium = fish; kennel = dogs.

questions.question: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'government' (govern + ment).

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error, or 'No error'.
Each of the students / have a book / in his hand.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so 'have' should be 'has'.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate preposition to fill in the blank.
He is good ______ mathematics.
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'good at' a subject or skill.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
I have lived in this town ______ ten years.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time (ten years); 'since' with a point of time.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate article to fill in the blank.
______ sun rises in the east.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used before unique objects such as the sun and the moon.

questions.question:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.
Rahul is writing a letter.
options: A letter is being written by Rahul.
A letter was being written by Rahul.
A letter is written by Rahul.
A letter has been written by Rahul.
questions.explanation: Present continuous active (is writing) becomes 'is being written' in the passive.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Physical fitness is important for everyone, but it is essential for those who serve in the armed and police forces. A fit body helps a soldier carry heavy loads, march long distances and stay alert during long hours of duty. Fitness, however, is not only about strength. A balanced diet, enough sleep and a calm mind are equally important. Many training centres now include yoga and meditation in their daily schedule, because they help trainees control stress and stay focused under pressure.

According to the passage, why is fitness essential for those who serve in the forces?
options: It helps them get promoted quickly
It helps them carry heavy loads, march long distances and stay alert
It allows them to avoid training
questions.explanation: The passage says a fit body helps a soldier carry heavy loads, march long distances and stay alert.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.
Author : Book :: Sculptor : ?
questions.explanation: An author creates a book; a sculptor creates a statue. The chisel is a tool and stone the material.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.
4 : 20 :: 6 : ?

Select the option that is related to the third letter-pair in the same way as the second letter-pair is related to the first letter-pair.
AC : FH :: KM : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves +5: A→F, C→H. So K→P, M→R.

questions.question: Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Hockey, football and cricket are outdoor field games; chess is a board game.

questions.question: Three of the following four numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 16, 25 and 36 are perfect squares; 45 is not.

questions.question: Three of the following four letter-pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd letter-pair.
questions.explanation: AZ, BY and CX are opposite-letter pairs (positions add to 27). D's opposite is W, not V.

questions.question:
Select the number that will come next in the following series.
1, 3, 7, 15, 31, ?
questions.explanation: Each term = previous × 2 + 1: 31 × 2 + 1 = 63.

questions.question:
Select the number that will come next in the following series.
100, 96, 88, 76, 60, ?
questions.explanation: Differences are −4, −8, −12, −16, so the next is 60 − 20 = 40.

questions.question:
Select the letter-cluster that will come next in the following series.
BCD, FGH, JKL, ?
questions.explanation: Each cluster starts 4 letters after the previous one: B, F, J, N → NOP.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'COLD' is written as 'DPME'. How will 'WARM' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is moved one place forward: W→X, A→B, R→S, M→N.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'BAT' is coded as 23. How will 'RAT' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Code = sum of alphabet positions: B2 + A1 + T20 = 23. RAT = 18 + 1 + 20 = 39.

questions.question: Pointing to a boy, Meena said, "He is the son of my only brother." How is the boy related to Meena?
questions.explanation: The son of one's brother is one's nephew.

questions.question: Starting from point P, Amit walks 4 km towards East, turns left and walks 3 km, and then turns left again and walks 4 km. How far and in which direction is he now from P?
questions.explanation: East 4 km, then North 3 km, then West 4 km cancels the eastward walk. He is 3 km North of P.

questions.question:
If '×' means '+', '+' means '−', '−' means '÷' and '÷' means '×', what is the value of the following expression?
18 − 3 ÷ 4 × 6 + 5

A square sheet of paper is folded once along its vertical middle line and then once along its horizontal middle line. A single hole is then punched through all the layers. How many holes will there be when the sheet is completely unfolded?
questions.explanation: Two folds make 4 layers, so one punch makes 4 holes.

questions.question: The Kalinga War was fought by which Mauryan ruler?
questions.explanation: Ashoka fought the Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE) and then turned to Buddhism. Samudragupta was a Gupta ruler.

questions.question: Who led the Salt Satyagraha march to Vedaranyam in Tamil Nadu in 1930?
questions.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari led the salt march from Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranyam in April 1930.

questions.question: India won the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 by defeating which team in the final?
questions.explanation: India beat New Zealand by four wickets in the final in Dubai on 9 March 2025.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India guarantees freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion?
questions.explanation: Article 25 (part of Articles 25–28, Right to Freedom of Religion).

questions.question: What is the term of office of a member of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha members serve 6-year terms; one-third retire every two years.

questions.question: The voting age in India was reduced from 21 years to 18 years by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 61st Amendment Act, 1988, lowered the voting age to 18.

questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.explanation: The Kosi, which floods and shifts its course often, is the 'Sorrow of Bihar'. The Damodar was called the 'Sorrow of Bengal'.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Rice is sown with the monsoon (Kharif); wheat, mustard and gram are Rabi crops.

questions.question: Lavani is a popular folk dance of which state?
questions.explanation: Lavani, performed to the beat of the dholki, is from Maharashtra.

questions.question: Which institution is known as the 'Banker's Bank' in India?
questions.explanation: The RBI keeps the reserves of commercial banks and lends to them, so it is the bankers' bank.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure electric current in a circuit?
questions.explanation: An ammeter measures current; a voltmeter measures potential difference.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of common salt?
questions.explanation: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.

questions.question: How many bones are there in the body of an adult human being?
questions.explanation: An adult has 206 bones; a newborn has about 300 that later fuse.

questions.question: The Ranji Trophy is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The Ranji Trophy is India's premier domestic first-class cricket championship.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the Border Security Force (BSF) located?

questions.question: What is the smallest number that must be subtracted from 1000 to make it exactly divisible by 7?
What is the unit digit of 4⁴⁵?
questions.explanation: Powers of 4 end in 4 (odd power) or 6 (even power). 45 is odd, so the unit digit is 4.

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 360. If one of the numbers is 72, what is the other number?
questions.explanation: Product of the numbers = HCF × LCM = 4320. Other number = 4320/72 = 60.

questions.question: What is the value of 25 × 4 ÷ 5 + 18 − 6 × 2?
What percentage of 250 is 45?
A student must obtain 40% of the total marks to pass. He gets 160 marks and fails by 40 marks. What are the maximum marks?
questions.explanation: Pass marks = 160 + 40 = 200 = 40% of total, so total = 500.

questions.question: A man buys a cycle for ₹2,500 and sells it for ₹2,800. What is his gain percentage?
A shopkeeper marks his goods 30% above the cost price and allows a discount of 10% on the marked price. What is his gain percentage?
At what rate of simple interest per annum will a sum of money double itself in 10 years?
questions.explanation: Interest = principal in 10 years, so rate = 100/10 = 10% per annum.

questions.question: What will be the amount on ₹5,000 after 2 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Amount = 5000 × 1.1 × 1.1 = ₹6,050. (₹6,000 is the simple-interest amount.)

questions.question: The ages of A and B are in the ratio 4 : 5. If the sum of their ages is 54 years, what is B's age?
questions.explanation: One part = 54/9 = 6, so B = 5 × 6 = 30 years.

questions.question: The average of five consecutive even numbers is 24. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: The middle number is the average, 24, so the numbers are 20, 22, 24, 26, 28. Largest = 28.

questions.question: 8 men can build a wall in 15 days. How many men will be needed to build the same wall in 10 days?
questions.explanation: M₁D₁ = M₂D₂: 8 × 15 = M × 10, so M = 12.

questions.question: A train 150 m long, running at 72 km/h, crosses a bridge in 20 seconds. What is the length of the bridge?
questions.explanation: 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Distance in 20 s = 400 m = train + bridge, so the bridge is 250 m.

questions.question: What is the area of a square whose diagonal is 12 cm?
questions.explanation: Area = d²/2 = 144/2 = 72 cm².

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.

Every year, thousands of young people join the armed forces and the police. Their training begins early in the morning with a run, followed by drill on the parade ground. Recruits learn to march in step, to handle equipment safely and to obey orders without delay. The training is hard, and many recruits feel tired and homesick during the first few weeks. Slowly, however, they grow stronger and more confident. They learn that discipline is not about fear but about trust: each member of a team must be able to depend on the others. By the end of the course, the recruits who once struggled with a short run can complete long marches carrying heavy loads.

What do the recruits do first every morning during training?
options: They do drill on the parade ground
They go on long marches with heavy loads
questions.explanation: 'Their training begins early in the morning with a run, followed by drill.'
